extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (biomedical, behavioral, social scientists) considering or preparing applications for the NIH Director's High‑Risk, High‑Reward Research awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility criteria for the NIH Common Fund High‑Risk, High‑Reward (HRHR) program and its four NIH Director's awards (Pioneer, New Innovator, Transformative Research, Early Independence). Useful for prospective applicants planning proposals and assessing fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program focus: exceptionally creative scientists pursuing highly innovative research with broad impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The High‑Risk, High‑Reward Research (HRHR) program supports exceptionally creative scientists pursuing highly innovative research with the potential for broad impact in biomedical, behavioral, or social sciences within the NIH mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program seeks scientists with high‑impact ideas that may be risky or at a stage too early to fare well in the traditional peer review process; it encourages creative, outside‑the‑box thinkers. Preliminary data are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research must fall within the NIH mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Supported projects must be in any area of biomedical, behavioral, or social science within the NIH mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Director's Pioneer Award — target and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For scientists with outstanding records of creativity pursuing pioneering approaches to major challenges; open to all career stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single PI only; research must be a new research direction; requires at least 51% research effort. Award level described as $700,000/year for 5 years (budget/term guidance). See the specific award website for application details and funding opportunity announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Director's New Innovator Award — target and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For exceptionally creative early career scientists proposing innovative, high‑impact projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must be an Early Stage Investigator (ESI). Single PI only; requires at least 25% research effort. Award level described as $475,000/year for 5 years. The page clarifies ESI status as investigators who are within 10 years of their final degree or post‑graduate clinical training and have not yet received a research project grant or equivalent NIH grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Director's Transformative Research Award — target and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotes cross‑cutting, interdisciplinary approaches; for individuals or teams proposing groundbreaking, unconventional research with the potential to create or challenge existing scientific paradigms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open to all career stages; open to individuals or teams; research effort should be commensurate with project needs. Flexible budget mechanism for up to 5 years (see award website for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Director's Early Independence Award — target and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides an opportunity for exceptional junior scientists who have recently received their doctoral degree or completed post‑graduate clinical training to bypass traditional postdoctoral training and move immediately into independent research positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must be a recipient of a terminal research degree or have completed postgraduate clinical training within the previous 16 months, or be expected to do so within the following 12 months of the application submission date. Single PI only; applicant must be in a non‑independent research position at time of application. Institutional limit: maximum of 2 Early Independence applications per institution. Award level described as $250,000/year for 5 years.
